*   **Primitive Index Map ($I_{id}$):** $\mathbb{Z}^{H \times W}$, storing the index of the primitive covering each pixel.

*   **Boundary Point Set ($B$):** A 2D set of pixel coordinates identified as boundary pixels (pixels with neighbors having different $I_{id}$ values).

The non-linear Bézier triangle surface is tessellated into smaller flat triangles to align with the pixel grid.

Pixels are marked as boundary pixels if they have neighboring pixels assigned to different primitive IDs.
At each computed 3D coordinate $\{\mathbf{S}_q\}$, a 3D Gaussian sub-primitive is generated on the fly.

*   The projected boundary radius $\sigma_i$ is computed for each boundary Gaussian.
